questions.q: What does the cloud block inside a terraform {} block do?
options: Replaces a backend block, connecting the configuration to a Terraform Cloud organization and workspace for remote state and runs
Installs the azurerm provider automatically
Creates a new terraform workspace with the CLI's workspace command
Converts HCL into ARM JSON for deployment
questions.explain: The cloud block replaces a backend block entirely — state storage and run execution move to Terraform Cloud instead of a self-managed backend.

questions.q: What concrete capability does Terraform Cloud add that running terraform apply from your own laptop doesn't have built in?
options: Automatic conversion of all resources into modules
A web UI that holds a run's plan output for a named human to review and approve before apply executes
A requirement to use AWS instead of Azure
The ability to write HCL using JSON syntax instead
questions.explain: Plain Terraform has no built-in review-before-apply UI; Terraform Cloud makes the plan output a reviewable, approvable artifact tied to a specific commit.

questions.q: What is Sentinel, in the context of Terraform Cloud and Terraform Enterprise?
options: A replacement for the terraform.tfvars file
The name of Terraform Cloud's VCS integration feature
A required provider for every Terraform configuration
HashiCorp's policy-as-code framework that can block a run between plan and apply if it violates a defined policy
questions.explain: A Sentinel policy runs between plan and apply and can hard-block a non-compliant run, such as one missing a required tag, before a human even reviews it.

questions.q: What is the key difference between Terraform Cloud and Terraform Enterprise?
options: Terraform Enterprise only supports AWS, while Terraform Cloud only supports Azure
Terraform Enterprise packages the same feature set to run self-hosted inside an organization's own network, for compliance/data-residency needs
Terraform Enterprise has fewer features than Terraform Cloud
There is no real difference between the two products
questions.explain: Terraform Enterprise is the self-hosted version of Terraform Cloud's model, aimed at organizations that can't send state or plan data to an external SaaS.

questions.q: Without Terraform Cloud or Terraform Enterprise, how does this course say a team can still get plan review and an apply approval gate?
options: It is not possible without a HashiCorp managed product
By writing a Sentinel policy, which only runs in plain open-source Terraform
By running terraform plan inside a regular CI/CD pipeline and building a manual approval step themselves, as Chapter 7 covers
By switching every environment to use workspaces instead of separate directories
questions.explain: Plain open-source Terraform remains a legitimate way to run production infrastructure; Chapter 7 shows how to build review and approval gates directly into a CI/CD pipeline instead.
